headline: Pertussis in Florida
blurb: Two Florida State Board of Health staff wrote that whooping cough killed more children than polio in Florida in 1955.

headline: Outbreak of Measles Following an Imported Case -- Florida
source: CDC, Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report
blurb: As of December 13, 1982, 203 confirmed measles cases had been reported from Dade County in an outbreak whose source was a 14-year-old who had vacationed in Peru.

headline: Measles -- Dade County, Florida
source: CDC, Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report
blurb: From July 14 through December 12, 1986, 258 confirmed measles cases were reported to the Dade County Department of Public Health.

headline: Effectiveness of a Seventh Grade School Entry Vaccination Requirement -- Statewide and Orange County, Florida, 1997-1998
source: CDC, Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report
blurb: Starting with the 1997-98 school year, Florida required students entering seventh grade to have hepatitis B vaccine, a second dose of MMR and a tetanus and diphtheria booster, and 61.8% were fully vaccinated by November 30, 1997.

headline: DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH, Appellant, v. Sara R. Johnson CURRY, and the Holmes County School Board, Appellees.
source: Florida First District Court of Appeal (Southern Reporter, via the Caselaw Access Project)
blurb: A Florida appeals court ruled that state law did not let the Department of Health question whether a parent's written religious objection to school immunizations was genuine.

headline: Notes from the Field: Outbreak of Pertussis in a School and Religious Community Averse to Health Care and Vaccinations — Columbia County, Florida, 2013
source: CDC, Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report
blurb: After whooping cough cases at a charter school where few kindergarten and seventh grade students were fully immunized, the Florida Department of Health in Columbia County declared a communicable disease emergency on September 12, 2013.

headline: Florida Surgeon General Scott A. Rivkees Issues Public Health Emergency in Response to Hepatitis A Outbreak
source: Florida Department of Health (archived by the Internet Archive)
blurb: Florida's surgeon general declared a public health emergency over the rise in hepatitis A cases and said vaccination is the best way to prevent infection.

headline: Florida plans to become first state to eliminate all childhood vaccine mandates
blurb: Florida's surgeon general announced plans to end vaccine mandates for children; some requirements can be ended by the state health department and others would need action by the legislature.
